what: The tenancy boundary, classified. One row per table in `packages/db/src/schema/`.
why: `AGENTS.md` states that `WORKSPACE_ID` is the only tenancy boundary in the system and that any new workspace-scoped read or write needs a cross-workspace isolation test. That rule was restated in five places — AGENTS.md, three `.kilo/agent/` personas, the `evidence-test` skill, and roughly forty rows of the findings ledger — and **none of them said which tables it applies to.** Without that list the rule cannot be evaluated in either direction: 'any new workspace-scoped write needs a test' has no way to decide whether a write is workspace-scoped, and 'do not add a table without `workspace_id`' has no way to know which tables that covers. This is the shape of `P-6`'s three startup-policy authorities and `P-5`'s two disagreeing `gate_status` lists; the remedy recorded for both was one source rather than five copies.
howToReadIt: `scope` is the **design decision**: does this table hold tenant-owned data (`workspace`) or not (`global`).
`column` is the **observed state**, committed so the gate can catch the boundary weakening. It is transcribed by a parser, not by hand.
`reason` says why this classification and state are acceptable today. A row without one is drift — `scripts/lib/tenancy-scope.mjs` fails it.

verifiedAgainstPostgres.how: A disposable `postgres:16-alpine` was started, the full 23-migration journal applied with `pnpm db:migrate`, and `pg_catalog` read directly rather than the TypeScript being parsed again.
verifiedAgainstPostgres.agreement: Exact, on all four numbers and on every individual table. PostgreSQL's own catalog returned the same 18 tables with the same nullability this register commits.
verifiedAgainstPostgres.whyThisMatters: **A parser checking a register the parser produced is self-consistent, not correct.** The register's `column` values are derived from the Drizzle schema by `scripts/lib/tenancy-scope.mjs`, so agreeing with itself proves nothing. Agreeing with `pg_catalog` after a real migration run is a different kind of evidence: it means the schema, the migration graph and this file all describe the same database. It also caught that all 23 migrations apply cleanly to an empty PostgreSQL 16, which nothing in the repository had asserted before.

whatBlocks: A table with no row here. A new table must be classified before it ships, which is when the decision is cheap.
A regression: a row committing `not-null` whose schema column is now nullable or gone.
A schema that improved past its row — a register wrong in the flattering direction is still wrong.
whatDoesNotBlock: Workspace-scoped tables without a hard boundary. That is real debt, counted and reported by `pnpm tenancy:check`, because failing on it would make the gate permanently red — and a permanently red gate stops catching the regressions above.

tally.note: **Derived, not asserted.** An earlier version of this file carried a hand-written tally of 19 / 37 / 18, which was wrong in every field — the numbers had been written from memory rather than measured. `scripts/lib/tenancy-scope.test.mjs` now recomputes all six from the schema and this register and fails if any disagree, so they cannot drift again. That is the `no-second-authority` failure this repository records as `P-6` and `P-5`, committed by the author of the skill that describes it.
tally.interpretation: Every workspace-scoped table carries a hard boundary since `0028_workspace_hard_boundaries.sql` (ledger MNT-17): `workspace_id` NOT NULL with a `restrict` key onto `workspaces` and an index leading with it. It was 25 absent and 3 nullable. `quality_gate_config` moved to `global` rather than being forced, because its NULL is the installation-wide default gate; see its row. The seven tables hard-scoped before MNT-17 by an unkeyed NOT NULL column (`schedules`, `outbox_events`, `conversations`, `messages`, `connector_configs`, `vault_entries`, `canonical_run_results`) gained the same `restrict` key in `0029_workspace_foreign_keys.sql` (ledger MNT-18), so every workspace-scoped table now names a workspace that exists.

installations.reason: The tenancy root. An installation IS the tenant boundary; a workspace column here would be a self-reference. This table is why `users`, `roles`, `sessions`, `service_credentials`, `installation_keys` and `saml_config` are `global` too — identity is installation-scoped, and stating that explicitly is the point of this file.

workspaces.reason: The workspace table itself. Its `id` is the value every `workspace_id` column points at, so it cannot also carry one.

saml_config.reason: Installation-level identity federation. One IdP configuration per installation.

users.reason: Installation-scoped identity, not workspace-scoped. A user belongs to an installation and holds a role per workspace in `workspace_members` (`0049_workspace_members.sql`), so the person is global and the role is the workspace's.

roles.reason: Installation-scoped identity. Role grants resolve against an installation and are then filtered per workspace by the caller, not by this table.

sessions.reason: Installation-scoped session. Same reasoning as `installation_keys`: authentication is not authorization.

service_credentials.reason: Installation-scoped credential, same as `api_keys`. Distinct from `connector_configs`, which IS workspace-scoped — see the note on that row, because the pair is the clearest case of two tables with near-identical names and opposite scoping.

installation_keys.reason: Keys for the installation itself, including the vault bootstrap key. Adding a workspace column would put a tenant boundary on the row that every tenant's vault depends on.

legacy_id_map.reason: Bookkeeping from the SQLite-to-Postgres migration. Its job is mapping old integer ids to new ones and it is not part of any product read path.

defect_categories.reason: Controlled vocabulary, shared by every tenant. The same category ids must mean the same thing across workspaces or cross-workspace reporting is meaningless.

fingerprint_categories.reason: A triage label is a team decision about its own failures: which cause is an environment problem, which is a known issue and where it is tracked. Global with no writer until `0048_triage_labels.sql` (ledger MKT-5), which scoped it with the hard boundary: `workspace_id` NOT NULL, a `restrict` key onto `workspaces`, and a primary key leading with it. Isolation: `apps/api/src/services/triage-label-service.test.ts`.

failure_taxonomy_rules.reason: Rules describing how failures are classified. Product configuration rather than tenant data, and the same rule set is intended to apply everywhere.

failure_classifications.reason: Classified failure records about a tenant-owned run. Hard-scoped by `0028_workspace_hard_boundaries.sql` (ledger MNT-17): NOT NULL, a `restrict` key onto `workspaces`, an index leading with it, and backfilled from its run's `workspace_id`, never from a caller.

failure_clusters.reason: Clusters of tenant-owned failures. Hard-scoped by `0028_workspace_hard_boundaries.sql` (ledger MNT-17), backfilled from the last or first run it was seen in; a cluster seen in runs of two workspaces has no single owner, so the migration raises rather than picking one. Dormant (see `docs/quality/capability-justification.md`).

test_failure_correlations.reason: Correlations between tenant-owned tests. Hard-scoped by `0028_workspace_hard_boundaries.sql` (ledger MNT-17), backfilled from `last_updated_run_id` where set and otherwise by the single-workspace rule; its uniqueness, which was global and let one tenant's correlation suppress another's, is now per workspace. Dormant (see `docs/quality/capability-justification.md`).

runs.reason: The central tenant-owned table. Its `workspace_id` was nullable with no key, so a run could belong to no workspace, invisible to every scoped read, or to one `workspaces` never registered. Hard-scoped by `0028_workspace_hard_boundaries.sql` (ledger MNT-17); every writer (the execution store, the reporter repository, the worker's scheduled `INSERT INTO runs`) sets it, and `DrizzleRunRepository` is now bound to one workspace and scopes every read and write. Isolation: `apps/api/src/repositories/run-repository-workspace-isolation.test.ts`, `apps/api/src/routes/execution.test.ts`.

runners.reason: Hard-scoped, and the composite `runners_workspace_name_unique` shows the constraint being applied to the multi-column shape rather than the single-column one.

canonical_run_results.reason: Hard-scoped, with the primary key itself declared as `(workspaceId, runId)` — the boundary in the key rather than in a column that can be null. Keyed onto `workspaces` with `restrict` by `0029_workspace_foreign_keys.sql` (ledger MNT-18), so the column names a workspace that exists.

artifacts.reason: Run evidence. Hard-scoped by `0028_workspace_hard_boundaries.sql` (ledger MNT-17), backfilled from the run; `addArtifact` takes the workspace from the run row, and every read filters on the artifact's own column. The run-scoped download route read an artifact by id with no workspace at all, so any workspace knowing two ids could download another's evidence; it is scoped now. Isolation: `apps/api/src/routes/execution.test.ts`.

Isolation: `apps/api/src/repositories/run-repository-workspace-isolation.test.ts`, `apps/api/src/routes/execution.test.ts`.

quality_gate_config.reason: **Installation configuration with optional per-workspace overrides, and `workspace_id` nullable by design.** NULL is a meaning, not a gap: it is the installation-wide default gate (id `global`) and every gate the dashboard creates, which `DrizzleQualityGateStore.add` writes deliberately. A hard boundary would turn the installation default into one workspace's private gate, so the column was **not** forced (ledger MNT-17). `global` is the register's only non-workspace scope and the accurate one for what the table is: product configuration whose default row no tenant owns. A row that does name a workspace is still bounded, since `0028_workspace_hard_boundaries.sql` added a `restrict` key onto `workspaces` and `quality_gate_config_workspace_project_idx` leads with the column. The gate still blocks if the column disappears, because `nullable` is committed here.
